highlights.title: Paramount will need to release way more movies to make this merger work
highlights.summary: Now that Paramount has reached a settlement with the 12 states that were suing to block its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), the studio is even closer to becoming one of the world's biggest production houses.
body: Paramount says it will release more films after merging with Warner Bros., but that promise may be difficult to keep.

Though the acquisition — which has not yet officially been finalized — would permanently fuse Paramount and WBD, the settlement only requires the newly merged company to adhere to a few rules for just five years. In the first two years, Paramount/WBD has to either put out 30 films annually or pay $30 million per film into healthcare and retirement funds managed by Hollywood’s biggest unions. During the following three years, the merged studio would need to release 32 films annually, and if it fails to meet any of these requirements during this five-year period, it will be forced to sell off its 49 percent stake in Miramax Studios to one of its competitors.

highlights.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
highlights.summary: Learn how GPT-6 improves prompt caching with higher cache hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls that reduce latency and costs.
body: Higher cache hit rates and new tools to help persistent agents run faster and cost less.

GPT‑6 enables persistent agents to work for hours on complex tasks, from refactoring codebases to producing well-researched documents and presentations. The applications behind these agents make a series of API requests that build on one another, often carrying forward the same instructions, tool definitions, and context from earlier turns. OpenAI caches that shared context to reuse computation across requests, reducing response times and giving developers discounts of up to 90% on cached input tokens.

With the GPT‑6 family, we launched an improved prompt caching system that delivers higher cache hit rates by default. We now give cache discounts for eligible shared prefixes reused within a 30-minute window. We’re also introducing new tools to help developers monitor cache performance, diagnose misses, and choose how much of a prompt to cache.

body: For Act One of Fortune's Weave, each of the game's four protagonists has a twelve-chapter story. By the time you get about partway through those chapters, your renown rank — one of several factors that allows you to recruit new teammates — starts climbing higher. Suddenly, buying the love of all those aloof prospects with swanky dinners at the inn and boatloads of fish sauce feels like a very real possibility. I spent the middle chapters of Leda's route scraping by while being underleveled, because I was more focused on expanding my team rather than improving it.

highlights.title: Rabbit’s new AI agent doesn’t need an R1 to run
highlights.summary: Rabbit, the company behind the underwhelming R1 device, is rolling out a standalone AI agent that you don't need its hardware to use, as reported earlier by Wired. The startup says its new OS3 "agentic operating system" runs in the cloud but operates locally across Windows, Mac, and Linux devices.
body: According to Rabbit, you can add up to five devices to one account, along with your preferred AI models. OS3 will automatically determine the devices, files, apps, and AI models it needs to complete a task. You can also access OS3 through its dedicated desktop site, a paired messaging app like Telegram or iMessage, as well as on Rabbit’s R1 device.

Though Rabbit founder Jesse Lyu tells Wired that the startup has stopped manufacturing R1 devices, it isn’t giving up on AI hardware entirely. It’s instead focusing on a new vibe-coding “cyberdeck” that will run OS3 when it launches within “months,” Wired reports.

Rabbit claims its OS3 system won’t store, copy, use, or sell your data. It notes that it will still keep your chats and memories stemming from them on its servers. Other AI providers linked to OS3 will also handle your data under their own privacy rules.

highlights.title: Woman's brain worm infection confirmed after eggs grow tails in lab test
highlights.summary: Out of nowhere, a woman's right arm and leg started shaking uncontrollably. In the moments leading up to the experience, she seemed well; she had no headache, confusion, or weakness. But for about a minute, half of her body juddered.
body: The woman, a rice farmer in the Philippines, headed to the emergency department. There, doctors gave her a physical exam and found nothing out of the ordinary. Then they took a look at her brain. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a bright cluster of nodules surrounded by fluid in her left frontal lobe. The doctors had an immediate guess as to what they were: worm eggs.

In a case report published in the latest issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, doctors write that they suspected the woman had neuroschistosomiasis, an uncommon complication of an infection with a Schistosoma parasitic worm, aka a blood fluke. In the Philippines, the most common fluke is S. japonicum. It's also found in China and part of Indonesia; despite its name, it has been eliminated from Japan.

highlights.title: Poitras Center to fuel early careers of 50 young scientists dedicated to psychiatric disorders research
highlights.summary: Patricia and James Poitras ’63 provide fellowships for graduate students and postdocs who will shape the future of mental health research.
body: Patricia and James Poitras ’63, longtime MIT supporters, have launched a fellowship program for graduate students and postdocs studying major mental illness, expanding their MIT philanthropy to directly support early-career scientists. The commitment establishes 50 two-year fellowships through the Poitras Center for Psychiatric Disorders Research at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research. Five fellowships will be awarded every year for the next decade, creating a long-term talent pipeline focused specifically on psychiatric disorders.

The $10 million gift is the latest in a series of philanthropic investments from the Poitras family to strengthen MIT’s capacity to address the growing burden of severe depression and anxiety, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and other complex psychiatric conditions. “Pat and Jim have remained steadfast in their decades-long commitment to bold research that can transform mental wellness,” says Robert Desimone, director of the McGovern Institute and head of the Poitras Center. “Their remarkable support of rising talent in the MIT ecosystem is yet another emblem of their commitment to that cause.”

highlights.title: Mahershala Ali Agrees That Kevin Feige Is a 'Gigantic Loser and Failure' Over Failed Blade Reboot
highlights.summary: Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali wholeheartedly agreed with Kevin Feige’s description of himself as a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting Marvel Studios’ canceled Blade reboot off the ground.
body: Feige made the remark on an episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast in late July, where he spoke about how excited he was to have Wesley Snipes reprise the role of Blade on Deadpool & Wolverine — an emotion that contrasted sharply with his failed attempts at making Ali’s reboot happen.

It turns out that Ali feels the same way. The actor admitted as much during a September 22 chat with GQ's Zach Baron, who cautiously broached the subject to see how Ali felt about the project now that it’s firmly in his rear view.

“That’s a Kevin Feige question,” he responded when asked why the film never moved forward. “They had, as you said, a two-time Oscar-winning actor under contract, and you got billions of dollars. …To this day, I don’t know why it didn’t happen. I just know that Kevin said it was the biggest failure of his career, and I agree.”
“I believe the quote was, ‘I feel like a giant loser and a failure,’” Baron suggested.

highlights.title: Skirts given star billing as Prada swerves trousers and dresses in Milan
highlights.summary: Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house. Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform is a knee-length skirt, A-line or pleated, most often with a plain sweater and kitten heels.
body: The Prada collection that opened Milan fashion week made a compelling case for her favourite outfit, with a skirt the star of every one of the 63 looks – no dresses, no trousers. It won the room over, so expect to see the personality skirt on a high street near you soon.

For the past six years, Miuccia Prada has shared design duties with Belgian designer Raf Simons, 20 years her junior. The arrangement was considered unusual when announced, but the house of Prada has always had a way of spinning gold from quirky ideas, and it has worked.
“She had the idea to focus on skirts this time,” Simons explained before this show. “And I said, why not make it an all-skirt show?”

She prefers skirts to dresses because “they give you room for contrast”, Mrs Prada said. “The way I think and feel is complicated, contradictory. If I wear something feminine, I want to wear something masculine too. A dress is all one idea, and we are never just one idea.”

highlights.title: How to Claim Your Cut of Apple’s $250 Million Siri Settlement
highlights.summary: Apple may pay out up to $95 for each eligible iPhone purchased by someone who felt misled about Siri’s release. You have until December 21 to submit a claim.
body: In May, Apple agreed to pay out $250 million as part of a class action lawsuit over claims the company overhyped its Apple Intelligence tools, specifically the long-delayed Siri AI overhaul.

Although the revamped Siri AI voice assistant is now available for owners of newer iPhones via iOS 27, you may still be eligible to claim cash back for past purchases. This settlement covers customers in the US who made their purchases from June 10, 2024 to March 29, 2025, and bought certain iPhone 15 or iPhone 16 models from Apple. If you qualify, you might receive up to $95 for each phone.

This settlement revolves around Apple’s promotion of Siri features to sell iPhones. “I expected to receive a Siri Apple Intelligence feature and did not receive it,” reads part of the statement you have to sign when filling out the claim form. As part of the settlement, Apple denies any wrongdoing.
“We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” read part of Apple’s statement from May about the settlement.

body: The Acer Nitro 85 gaming PC is equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 8700F CPU, GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB M.2 SSD. The Ryzen 7 8700F is an 8-core, 16-thread processor with a max boost clock of 5.1GHz. It's not the fastest or newest AMD CPU, but it's still a solid gaming CPU that won't bottleneck the GPU, especially at the higher resolutions you should be playing at if you own a 5070 Ti. It's cooled by a robust tower heatsink fan.

The GeForce RTX 5070 is the best Nvidia card for 1080p and 1440p gaming and by itself this card retails for $600 (although generally it's higher these days). It's also powerful enough to run most games at 4K, although at that point you'll see noticeable gains jumping up to a 5070 Ti. Compared to the previous generation GPUs, the RTX 5070 offers a slight performance improvement over the RTX 4070 Super, which was and still is an excellent GPU. The fps gain is greater in games that support DLSS 4.5 with multi-frame generation. Check out our RTX 5070 review.

body: According to Jane Rosenthal, three words can change an aspiring filmmaker’s life. She wasn’t referring to Through Her Lens —although Tribeca and Chanel’s long-running program for women and non-binary auteurs can and does do just that. Rather, she was reminding a room full of powerful people—actors, directors, and executives—to just “read the script” when they are given an opportunity to do so.

The CEO of Tribeca, who started her career in 1975 as one of very few women in the room, recalled a formative moment when she fought hard to bring a project about domestic violence to the screen, despite numerous objections. The movie in question, based on a true story, ended up being The Burning Bed, with Farrah Fawcett playing the lead. Not only did it win awards; it prompted national conversation around the pervasive issue once it saw the light of day. “That moment taught me something very early on: It matters who is in the room. It matters even more who has the power, and who is willing to say, “Yes. Read the script. Listen to her.”

highlights.title: Cities across US oppose Trump FCC plan to preempt local broadband rules
highlights.summary: Cities and counties around the US are angry at the Trump administration over a proposal to override local rules that govern the deployment of wired broadband networks.
body: The Federal Communications Commission has been taking public comments on a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking that proposes to preempt state and local permitting rules. The FCC argues that too many local governments “excessively delay approvals and seek to extract exorbitant sums from providers, resulting in costs that render some deployments infeasible.”

The FCC plan is supported by broadband providers, but local governments told the FCC that it would override rules that protect public safety. Local governments say the plan is illegal and that the FCC should instead focus on how Internet providers thwart competition with permit-hoarding and other tactics that prevent competitors from deploying networks.

The FCC docket has drawn many comments from leaders of individual municipalities, and from groups representing local governments nationwide. They object to FCC plans to impose a 120-day deadline for processing permits and to proposed limits on fees and compensation that local governments can require from providers.

highlights.title: Halo Studios Cinematic Director Promoted and Laid Off Within the Same Week as Xbox's Brutal Restructuring Continues
highlights.summary: Halo Studios cinematic director Josh Daniels has confirmed that he was promoted and laid off within the same week amid news that Activision has now taken over development of the next Halo game.
body: Xbox’s big restructuring continues this week, with Chief Content Officer Matt Booty announcing 268 layoffs "across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer.”

One of the employees impacted by these layoffs was Josh Daniels, the now-former cinematic director of Halo Studios. He confirmed the news in a post on LinkedIn, where he revealed that he’d just gotten promoted that same week in a brutal turn of events.

“Promoted and laid off in the same week is pretty wild. I'm one of the many hit by the Halo Studios layoffs,” he wrote. “I'll be taking some offline time today, but very much would love to talk to anyone looking for Cinematic Direction or Production roles. Feel free to get in touch if anything looks like I might be a fit.”

Daniels had been involved with Xbox for just over a decade, having previously lent his talents to the Forza Motorsport games. He was anointed cinematic director at Halo Studios in 2024 and worked on Halo: Campaign Evolved, a title that was met with a lukewarm reception from players upon its release earlier this year.
points: Halo Studios cinematic director Josh Daniels has confirmed that he was promoted and laid off within the same week amid news that Activision has now taken over development of the next Halo game.

highlights.summary: The Thomas Guide Is a map that painstakingly details how to navigate Los Angeles by car. It’s a spiral-bound relic that almost none of your junior executives remember. Your assistant thinks it’s a ranking of pale British heartthrobs.
body: I’ll tell my assistants — not my current two, because they’ve gotten it — but I ask them to call [someone] and I’ll follow up and ask if they talked to them. The assistants will say, “Well, I texted.” But that’s not what I asked for. I asked you to call. I understand that texts and DMs are how we have the conversation now, but I like the personal [nature] of a phone call. I’ll also have my assistant call back after 15-20 minutes. They’ll say, “We just left word.” Call again!

The overall content business — from live sports to live events, movies, TV, podcasts, social, concerts, books, lectures — it’s all going to expand. I also think we’ll see more production … and costs will come down because of AI. The creators will keep making small movies that make a lot of money [like “Obsession”]. You’re going to start seeing a lot of new development around that. Steve Jobs [once spoke about] a study about humans. That they were the slowest-moving mammals until the invention of the bicycle, then became the fastest. So, whatever [Hollywood looks like in the future], we’ll still need legs to pedal those bikes.

highlights.title: Andreessen Horowitz is launching an ‘academy’ with no homework and partnerships with Palantir, Google, and Meta
highlights.summary: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an "academy" positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The "Horowitz Andreessen Academy" will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI…
body: The Horowitz Andreessen Academy trades degrees and homework for stints at tech companies.

To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of [their] time working and exploring.”

The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.

highlights.title: It's Officially the End of an Era For Halo
highlights.summary: Halo will never be the same. On Tuesday, Xbox announced the next phase of its ongoing restructuring, with a memo from executive vice president Matt Booty citing developer Halo Studios as the first line item in a wave of 268 new job cuts.
body: This is the sort of news that, a decade ago, would have sounded like a prank. But in 2026 — where golf course moguls can be two-term presidents and Silicon Valley can actively engineer the end of humanity with no blowback whatsoever — it’s business as usual. For Xbox specifically, it’s another chapter in a decade of brand mismanagement, and a symbolic end to one of gaming’s longtime fanbase wars.

Halo, of course, has been the face of Xbox since the very beginning. Bungie’s 2001 shooter Halo: Combat Evolved was arguably the game that moved original Xbox consoles. Its successors, 2004’s Halo 2 and 2007’s Halo 3, are still considered some of the best first-person shooters ever made, as close to universally beloved as video games get. Even the spinoffs, like Halo: Reach, were extremely well-regarded.

“Digger” stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy tycoon who must save the world when one of his oil rigs malfunctions and causes an environmental catastrophe across the planet. The film’s supporting cast includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons.

For Cruise, “Digger” notably marks his return to adult-oriented drama after more than a decade playing action movie heroes. In the last 10 years, Cruise’s only non-action movie is the 2017 crime comedy “American Made.” One would have to go back 20 years to add more non-action movies to Cruise’s roster, such as the musical “Rock of Ages,” the political drama “Lions for Lambs,” the comedy “Tropic Thunder” and the historical thriller “Valkyrie.” Cruise’s return to more dramatic fare has raised the eyebrows of Oscar pundits since “Digger” was announced a few years ago, but the wildly divisive reactions to “Digger” may upend his expected awards campaign.

highlights.title: The Best Boxed Stuffing Mix, According to Our Taste Test
highlights.summary: We tasted seven popular stuffing mixes from Stove Top, Pepperidge Farm, Trader Joe’s, and more. These three came out on top.
body: Boxed stuffing may not taste exactly like homemade stuffing, but when Thanksgiving prep starts to feel chaotic, a good mix is a shortcut worth taking.

The best boxed stuffing should have the hallmarks of a great homemade version: a soft, fluffy interior, a crisp, bronzed top, and plenty of buttery, savory flavor. We looked for mixes with distinct pieces of bread that absorbed moisture without turning soggy or stodgy, plus enough sage, rosemary, parsley, and other aromatics to make every bite taste like Thanksgiving.

We tested seven popular boxed stuffing mixes to find the ones worth serving. Stove Top Savory Herbs was our favorite overall, Stove Top Traditional Sage was the herbiest, and Pepperidge Farm Herb-Seasoned Classic Stuffing had the freshest flavor and texture.

The clear favorite in our taste test, Stove Top Savory Herbs has an ingredient list similar to our runner up, Stove Top Traditional Sage with one noteworthy difference. Savory Herbs includes MSG, which gives this mix its extra savory boost.
